name: Kaitumjaure-Teusajaure
estimatedTime: 3-5 or 4-5 hours depending on official source

difficulty.label: Mostly easy fell stage with rocky, exposed and steep sections
difficulty.source: STF and Naturkartan describe a short stage that is mostly easy/open fell walking, but both official text and field reports note stone/rock near the start, possible wet sections, limited water on Muorki and a steep rocky final descent to Teusajaure.
caveats: STF route overview lists 4-5 hours while the STF section page/Naturkartan lane reported 3-5 hours.
AllTrails reviewers called the segment easy, but blogs and field reports call the climb/descent rocky, stony, tiring or weather-dependent.
Wind on the plateau and wind/waves at Teusajaure can materially change the practical difficulty even when the footpath is passable.

camping.summary: Camping evidence is good but should be represented as section context rather than exact campsite POIs except at hut areas. Naturkartan identifies good tent pitches above Kaitumjaure cabins, along Gaidumjohka and north of Muorki. Field reports mention useful spots above Teusajaure and higher in the hills before paid lakeside camping.
specificNotes: No formal mid-section campsite with verified coordinates was found.
Ordinary individual tenting was not found to be banned for this stage, but Sjaunja/Laponia etiquette and reserve rules matter.
Avoid private huts/katas, paths, sensitive moss/lichen ground and reindeer enclosures; do not camp next to reindeer work areas.
Organized camps or large recurring group activities in Sjaunja require Lansstyrelsen permission according to the rules lane.

shelter.summary: The only mid-section shelter-like feature in official text is the kata about 4 km south of Kaitumjaure; coordinate and current usability need verification before import.

fire.summary: Treat open fires as restricted. Laponia guidance says fires are allowed only at designated fireplaces within the World Heritage, and Sjaunja rules prohibit damaging or taking living/dead trees and shrubs. No standalone route fireplace was verified for section 7.
caveats: Check Gallivare/Norrbotten fire-ban status immediately before public use.
Hut kitchens/saunas/firewood chores should be folded into hut metadata, not standalone route fireplaces.

rules: Dogs: Sjaunja rules prohibit loose dogs; Laponia guidance allows dogs in Sjaunja only if leashed. Keep dogs leashed and under control.
Reindeer: active reindeer husbandry is flagged by STF and Sjaunja rules prohibit intentional disturbance of grazing, gathering or driving reindeer. Detour or wait rather than approaching herds.

Drones: Laponia says drone flights are forbidden throughout Laponia without County Administrative Board permission. Older reserve aircraft rules may vary by subarea; apply the stricter Laponia rule unless confirmed otherwise.
Fire: Laponia allows fires only at designated fireplaces within the World Heritage; Sjaunja rules prohibit damaging or taking vegetation/wood. Check active fire bans before any stove/open flame use.

Camping: ordinary individual tenting was not found to be specifically banned, but organized camps/large recurring group activities require permission and all camping should avoid sensitive ground, reindeer infrastructure and private katas/huts.

Fishing: Lansstyrelsen manages state waters above the cultivation line; permits and Gallivare 2026 rules apply. Running-water and grayling closures may be date-specific, and Suorkejokk/Teusajaure has special/quota-rule context.

Hunting: Sjaunja generally restricts hunting with permit exceptions by subarea; 2025-2026 small-game season was reported as ended by 2026-04-29. Recheck 2026-2027 rules for late-August/September travel.
safetyNotes: The route reaches exposed high plateau around 780 to just over/under 800 m; SMHI bare-mountain wind warnings can be relevant at this elevation.
Water is scarce on Muorki/high plain; fill before the climb.
The final kilometer to Teusajaure is steep and rocky and is worse in rain.
The Kaitumjakka/Gaidumjohka bridge is a known structure; field reports call it bouncy but no current bridge-out notice was found.
Teusajaure boat/rowboat crossing is outside section 7 mainline but can affect access and continuation; wind can make rowing unsafe or impossible.
No mobile coverage is reported at Kaitumjaure or Teusajaure huts.
currentness: No Kaitumjaure-Teusajaure-specific closure, reroute or bridge-out notice was found in Lansstyrelsen current mountain information as accessed 2026-04-29.

Lansstyrelsen posted a countywide 2026-04-22 winter-route notice that route checks had stopped because warmth worsened snow/ice and made some crossings unsafe; treat as a spring/winter warning, not a summer trail closure.
STF Kaitumjaure and STF Teusajaure 2026 staffed/open periods were reported as 2026-02-27 to 2026-04-19 and 2026-06-18 to 2026-09-13.
On 2026-04-29 both huts were between staffed seasons; expect only emergency/safety space rather than staffed service.
Krisinformation fire-ban map text was reported updated 2026-04-08; live fire-ban status must be checked immediately before use.

observations: After rain, Kaitumjakka was high/fast and the Gaidumjohka chain bridge felt bouncy but usable.
Route had a long rocky gradual ascent, exposed cold wind on the high point and a steep descent beside a cascading stream to Teusajaure.
Free camping was signed higher in the hills; lakeside camping had a fee.
Teusajaure had shop snacks, water, tent pitches and boat booking through the hut/shop.

observations: Reverse direction report said wind and waves made Teusajaure rowing impossible and the hut keeper ferried only limited groups.

Notes hut area in lush forest near rocky lakeshore.
Combines this section with the Teusajaure crossing and Vakkotavare approach.
